title: Comparing Janitorial Quotes & Contracts: RFP Scorecards, COI Audits & Red Flags

metaDescription: Comparing janitorial quotes & contracts: audit 4.333-week billing, $35–$65/hr labor, COI limits & exclusions. Run our calculator or compare vendor bids.
excerpt: Learn how US facility managers normalize competing commercial cleaning bids down to implied labor hours, 4.333-week monthly visit math, and exact scope inclusions. Use this RFP scorecard, COI verification checklist, and contract red-flag guide to select a reliable W-2 contractor without overpaying.
quickAnswer: Comparing janitorial quotes & contracts requires normalizing every bid to implied labor hours ($35 to $65/hr standard W-2 rates) and exact annual visits divided by 12 using 4.333 weeks per month (13.0 visits/month for 3x/week; 21.65 for 5x/week). For a 10,000 sq ft mixed-floor office with four restrooms cleaned 3x/week, credible labor-only quotes benchmark at $9,857 to $17,121 per month ($758 to $1,317/visit), rising to $12,068 to $21,751/month when breakrooms, interior glass, paper/soap consumables, and quarterly deep floor care are included.

blocks.text: Soliciting three commercial cleaning proposals for the exact same suite routinely produces quotes separated by 40% to 60%. On paper, every vendor promises sparkling restrooms, spotless breakrooms, and dependable evening crews—making it tempting for finance teams to rubber-stamp the lowest monthly retainer.

In practice, wide price gaps rarely reflect one company being dramatically more efficient. Instead, they expose differences in **W-2 payroll compliance vs. 1099 subcontracting**, **4-week vs. 4.333-week visit billing**, **hidden scope exclusions**, and **unrealistic labor-hour budgets**. This procurement hub brings together our RFP frameworks, insurance verification standards, and bid-scoring rules so you can audit every line item apples to apples.
Why Office Cleaning Quotes Differ by 40% to 60% for Identical Floor Plans

Before judging any proposal expensive or cheap, verify that all bidders priced the exact same cleanable footprint and task matrix. As outlined in our guide on [how to compare 3 office cleaning quotes and mistakes to avoid](/comparing-quotes-and-contracts/how-to-compare-3-office-cleaning-quotes-mistakes-to-avoid/), mismatched assumptions around breakroom appliances, conference glass partitions, consumables, and floor restoration account for most quote variance.

Equally common is **labor-hour compression**. Using ISSA commercial cleaning production averages (~**3,500 sq ft per labor hour**, typically **2,800 to 4,000 sq ft/hr** plus **0.15 to 0.25 hours per restroom**), a **10,000 sq ft office with four restrooms** requires **3.10 to 4.57 technician hours per visit**. A vendor quoting $5,000/month for 3x/week service in a market where compliant W-2 janitorial billing runs **$35 to $65 per hour** can only survive by cutting shift time in half or offloading rooms to uninsured 1099 subcontractors.
Normalizing Competing Bids: The 4.333-Week and Labor-Hour Audit

Every commercial contract must convert weekly frequency into annual visits divided by 12 using **4.333 weeks per month** (**13.0 visits/month** for 3x/week; **21.65 visits/month** for 5x/week). Vendors who price a 3x/week contract on 12 visits/month quietly skip fifth-week service days or tack on supplemental charges four times a year.

The audit table below compares three real-world bid structures for a **10,000 sq ft mixed-floor office** (**1.05x** flooring multiplier, **4 restrooms**, **3x/week = 13.0 visits/month**). Using national benchmarks (**$0.07 to $0.12/sq ft** base rate, **$15 to $30/restroom**, **0.95x** 3x/week multiplier), a compliant labor-only contract totals **$758 to $1,317/visit ($9,857 to $17,121/month)**, while a turnkey full-scope contract totals **$905 to $1,627/visit ($12,068 to $21,751/month)**.

blocks.title: Spot Red Flags Using Implied Hourly Math
blocks.text: Divide each bidder's per-visit price by your ISSA labor-hour estimate (3.10 to 4.57 hours for 10,000 sq ft with 4 restrooms). Whenever the implied billing rate falls below $30 to $35 per hour in a standard US metro, the vendor cannot pay legal W-2 wages, FICA/FUTA taxes, and Workers' Compensation while turning a profit—making missed shifts or 1099 misclassification almost inevitable.

blocks.text: Never sign an agreement until every common exclusion has a clear yes/no assignment and unit price attached in your [janitorial scope of work checklist](/comparing-quotes-and-contracts/janitorial-scope-of-work-checklist/). Across US office contracts, four add-ons routinely separate lean base bids from turnkey packages:

items: **Breakroom & Kitchenette Sanitation ($12 to $25 per visit):** Covers sink scrubbing, countertop disinfection, microwave interior/exterior wipe-downs, refrigerator fronts, and cabinet pulls; usually excludes inside-fridge cleanouts.

**Interior Glass & Conference Partitions ($15 to $35 per visit):** Covers entry glass sidelights and full-height conference room partitions; exterior second-story window washing remains a separate specialty contract.

**Paper, Soap & Trash Liner Consumables ($0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit):** For a 10,000 sq ft suite, expect **$120 to $250 per visit** when vendor-supplied; audit dispenser lock-in contracts carefully before bundling.

**Quarterly Deep Floor Care ($0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month):** Amortizes hot-water carpet extraction, VCT scrub-and-recoat, or ceramic grout scrubbing instead of paying **$55 to $95 per specialty hour** ad hoc.

blocks.text: Insurance, Bonding, and W-2 vs. 1099 Compliance Verification

Risk transfer is the primary reason commercial tenants hire outside vendors rather than hiring casual labor. Yet an alarming share of cheap proposals rely on misclassified independent contractors—a vulnerability detailed in our breakdown of [1099 subcontractors vs. W-2 cleaning crews](/comparing-quotes-and-contracts/1099-subcontractors-vs-w2-cleaning-crews/) and [red flags in cheap cleaning quotes](/comparing-quotes-and-contracts/red-flags-in-cheap-cleaning-quotes/). If an uninsured cleaner slips on a wet stairwell or walks off with a master keycard, your property insurer and state labor board can look directly to your company for damages.

blocks.title: Mandatory COI, Bonding, and OSHA Clauses Before First Key Handoff
blocks.text: Follow our insurance audit guide on verifying janitorial general liability coverage: collect a Certificate of Insurance directly from the vendor's broker showing $1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate CGL naming your entity and landlord as Additional Insured, statutory Workers' Compensation covering all on-site staff, and a $25,000–$100,000 janitorial fidelity bond. Require written compliance with OSHA HazCom (29 CFR 1910.1200) SDS labeling and OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030) protocols for restroom bio-hazards.
Contract Terms, CPI Escalation Caps, and Facility Hardware Standards

Fine print inside a service agreement often matters more in months 7 through 24 than the initial monthly rate. As explained in our analysis of [CPI price escalation clauses](/comparing-quotes-and-contracts/cpi-price-escalation-clauses-explained/), multi-year contracts should cap annual increases at the lesser of local CPI or 3% to 4% (excluding documented statutory minimum-wage ordinances), grant a **30-day termination-for-convenience clause** after a 14-day cure notice, and establish automatic invoice credits for verified missed visits.

Your contract scope should also standardize waste-station and cart hardware so crews work efficiently without damaging suite finishes or leaving unlocked chemicals in public corridors. In tight copy rooms and breakrooms, specifying narrow containers like the **Rubbermaid Commercial Slim Jim 23-Gallon Recycling & Waste Station** (`23 gal` capacity, `Vent Channels` that cut liner pull effort, `11-in Wide` profile, `Bag Cinches`) prevents torn bags and wall scuffs. In Class A lobbies and elevator banks, architectural bins like the **Safco Public Square 37-Gallon Commercial Steel Receptacle** (`37 gal` capacity, `Fire-Safe Steel` construction, `Square Profile`, `Liner Retainer`) protect fire-code compliance, while daytime porters should stage supplies inside an enclosed unit such as the **Suncast Commercial Housekeeping Cart with Locking Cabinet** (`Locking Doors`, `300 lb Cap` load rating, `8-in Wheels`, `Bag Holder`) paired with quiet commercial vacuums reviewed in our [Sanitaire SC888N vs. Oreck XL2100RHS comparison](/commercial-vacuums-and-floor-machines/sanitaire-tradition-sc888n-vs-oreck-xl2100rhs/).

blocks.title: Eliminate 12-to-36-Month Evergreen Auto-Renewal Windows
blocks.text: Many national and franchise janitorial agreements lock clients into 12-to-36-month terms that automatically renew unless cancelled by certified mail 60 to 90 days before expiration. Strike evergreen clauses before signing and insist on a mutual 30-day written cancellation clause after an initial 60-day onboarding window.
6-Step Contract Award and Walkthrough Audit Checklist

Use this six-step procurement sequence alongside our [how to verify janitorial general liability insurance](/comparing-quotes-and-contracts/how-to-verify-janitorial-general-liability-insurance/) and [how to compare 3 office cleaning quotes](/comparing-quotes-and-contracts/how-to-compare-3-office-cleaning-quotes/) guides before issuing your next award letter.

items.name: Standardize Your RFP Scope Matrix
items.text: Send all bidders identical net cleanable square footage, flooring breakdowns, restroom counts, and breakroom/glass task frequencies so bids reflect true rate differences rather than guesswork.

items.name: Run Pre-Bid Walkthroughs With Facility Leads
items.text: Walk every shortlisted vendor through security check-in, freight elevators, janitorial closets, and high-soil lobbies so no bidder claims surprise access constraints after launch.

items.name: Normalize Monthly Totals to 4.333 Weeks and ISSA Hours
items.text: Convert every monthly price into per-visit dollars (dividing by 13.0 for 3x/week or 21.65 for 5x/week) and audit implied hourly labor against $35–$65/hr US benchmarks.

items.name: Verify Broker-Issued COIs and W-2 Payroll Status
items.text: Confirm Additional Insured CGL ($1M/$2M), statutory Workers' Compensation, and fidelity bonding directly with the issuing insurance agency before granting badge access.

items.name: Separate Consumables and Deep Floor Care Line Items
items.text: Compare vendor-supplied paper/soap ($0.012–$0.025/sq ft/visit) and quarterly floor care ($0.03–$0.06/sq ft/mo) against direct procurement so markups stay transparent.

faqs.q: What Certificates of Insurance (COI) must a US janitorial contractor provide?
faqs.a: Require a broker-issued Certificate of Insurance listing at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate Commercial General Liability naming your company and property landlord as Additional Insured, statutory Workers' Compensation covering W-2 technicians, Commercial Auto if vehicles enter loading docks, and a janitorial fidelity or employee dishonesty bond.

faqs.q: Why should every cleaning contract specify 4.333 weeks per month instead of 4 weeks?
faqs.a: Because a 52-week year averages 4.333 weeks per month, a 3x/week schedule equals 13.0 visits per month and a 5x/week schedule equals 21.65 visits per month. Contracts written on a 4-week month (12 or 20 visits) either omit fifth-week cleanings or bill surprise extra-day charges.

faqs.q: Does requiring Green Seal GS-37 or EPA Safer Choice chemicals raise bid prices?
faqs.a: Usually by 0% to 4% when contractors use automated wall-mounted chemical dilution dispensers, which cut concentrate waste. Larger cost differences in LEED green cleaning addenda stem from specifying certified HEPA backpack vacuums and microfiber laundering rather than the chemicals themselves.

faqs.q: Which high-cost tasks are normally excluded from standard janitorial quotes?
faqs.a: Base square-footage quotes exclude hot-water carpet extraction, VCT floor stripping and waxing, exterior window washing, high dusting above 8 to 10 feet, inside-refrigerator cleanouts, paper and soap consumables ($0.012–$0.025/sq ft/visit), and biohazard remediation regulated under OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030), which typically bill at $55 to $95 per specialty hour.

faqs.q: What notice period and CPI cap should I negotiate in a commercial cleaning contract?
faqs.a: Aim for a 30-day termination-for-convenience clause (after a 14-day written cure period for service deficiencies) rather than a 12-to-36-month auto-renewing lock-in, and cap annual CPI price escalations at 3% to 4% unless a documented local minimum-wage ordinance forces higher direct payroll.
